name: Cimetidine
route_note: Oral tablets or solution; injection in some markets
originator: Smith, Kline & French (Welwyn Garden City, UK)

discovery.by: James Black, Robin Ganellin, Graham Durant and colleagues at SK&F
discovery.note: A product of rational drug design, developed from histamine via burimamide and metiamide.

tagline: First H2 blocker and first 'blockbuster', born of rational drug design
summary: Cimetidine was the first histamine H2-receptor antagonist and transformed peptic ulcer treatment in the late 1970s. A landmark of rational drug design, it became the first drug to reach US$1 billion in annual sales, but its inhibition of liver enzymes causes many drug interactions.
mechanism: Cimetidine competitively blocks H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, reducing histamine-stimulated acid secretion, especially at night.

Its imidazole ring binds the haem iron of several cytochrome P450 enzymes (CYP1A2, 2C9, 2D6, 3A4), inhibiting metabolism of warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin and others. It also has weak anti-androgenic activity, which can cause gynaecomastia.

history.title: H2 receptor programme
history.detail: James Black's team at SK&F begins searching for antagonists of histamine's acid-stimulating effect.

history.title: H2 receptor defined
history.detail: The team reports burimamide and the existence of H2 receptors; cimetidine is synthesised the same year.

history.title: UK launch
history.detail: Tagamet is launched in the United Kingdom.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: James Black shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, partly for the discovery of cimetidine and propranolol.

history.title: OTC
history.detail: Tagamet HB is approved for non-prescription use in the US.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic (sulfoxide and hydroxymethyl metabolites); inhibits several CYPs

serious: Drug interactions through CYP inhibition (warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin)
Gynaecomastia and impotence at high doses

facts: Cimetidine is often cited as the first 'blockbuster' drug.
The 1972 Nature paper describing H2 receptors was based on burimamide, cimetidine's predecessor.
